images.caption: Figure 1:HOG-WAM architecture and real-robot performance.Left.An auxiliary HOG DiT provides future-gradient supervision to the RGB backbone through asymmetric mixed attention during training. Language and proprioception condition all three DiT modules through cross-attention. Inference uses the RGB and action modules. Snowflakes and flames mark frozen and trainable components, and×30\times 30denotes transformer depth. VAE denotes variational autoencoder, FFN feed-forward network, and Proj. projection.Right.FastWAM and HOG-WAM success rates on four Franka manipulation tasks under clean and noisy observations, with 25 trials per task, model, and condition. Noise follows the RoboTwin-Plus mixed-noise operator.

Figure 2:Construction of future-gradient supervision. Demonstration frames provide deterministic structural targets, encoded by the same frozen VAE as RGB. The HOG DiT predicts velocities over noisy HOG latents, and future frames contribute to the auxiliary loss. Monochrome gradients illustrate local boundaries; the three-channel training raster followsEq.2.

Figure 4:Franka manipulation tasks. Columns show bracket reorientation, produce placement, block stacking, and cylinder insertion. The upper row contains initial main-camera RGB observations from recorded demonstrations; the lower row shows gradients of the same images. These monochrome displays illustrate local boundaries; training uses the HOG-derived raster defined inSec.3.2.

images.caption: Figure S1:RoboTwin visual-corruption extension (RoboTwin-Plus). Clean observations are shown separately from the four corruption conditions. A single corruption operator modifies the RGB observation before visual encoding, preserving the manipulation objective and nonvisual conditioning. Mixed noise, warm filtering, underexposure, and reduced contrast probe complementary forms of visual distribution shift. Each completed evaluation comprises 50 tasks with 100 valid episodes per task, model, and condition; the RoboTwin-Plus score averages success across the four conditions.
